name: Skeletal system
description: The bones of the body and how they fit together: the skeleton as a whole, bone tissue, the skull, the vertebral column, the thorax, the limbs and the joints. Picture questions show the skeleton with one bone highlighted to name.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: How many bones are in the adult human skeleton?
questions.explanation: A newborn has about 270 to 300 bony pieces; many fuse during growth (the skull, sacrum and hip bones, for example), leaving 206.

figure.alt: The whole skeleton from the front
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many bones make up the axial skeleton?
questions.explanation: Skull 22, ear ossicles 6, hyoid 1, vertebral column 26 and thorax 25 (24 ribs and the sternum).

questions.prompt: How many bones make up the appendicular skeleton?
questions.explanation: The two girdles and the limbs: 64 in the shoulders and upper limbs, 62 in the hips and lower limbs. 80 + 126 = 206.

questions.prompt: Which division of the skeleton is made up of the skull, the vertebral column and the rib cage?
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton is the central axis of the body: it protects the brain, spinal cord and organs of the chest.

figure.alt: The whole skeleton from the front, with the axial skeleton in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which division of the skeleton is made up of the limbs and the girdles that attach them?
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton is the “appendages”: arms, legs, and the shoulder and hip girdles.

figure.alt: The whole skeleton from the front, with the appendicular skeleton in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Name two functions of the skeleton.
questions.explanation: Support, protection, movement (as levers for muscles), making blood cells in red marrow, and storing minerals (calcium and phosphate) and fat (in yellow marrow).

questions.prompt: What is the longest and strongest bone in the body?
questions.explanation: The femur is about a quarter of your height.

figure.alt: The legs from the front, with the right femur in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the smallest bone in the body?
questions.explanation: The stapes, one of the three ossicles of the middle ear, is about 3 mm long.

questions.prompt: What type of bone is longer than it is wide, like the femur, the humerus or a phalanx?
questions.explanation: Long bones have a shaft (diaphysis) and two ends (epiphyses). Even the little phalanges are long bones.

questions.prompt: The carpals and tarsals are examples of which type of bone?
questions.explanation: Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, about as wide as they are long.

questions.prompt: The sternum, ribs, scapulae and the bones of the skull roof are which type of bone?
questions.explanation: Flat bones are thin plates, often curved, that protect organs and give muscles a broad attachment.

questions.prompt: The vertebrae are which type of bone?
questions.explanation: Irregular bones have complex shapes that fit no other group. The hip bones and some skull bones (sphenoid, ethmoid) are irregular too.

questions.prompt: What is a bone that develops inside a tendon, like the kneecap, called?
questions.explanation: “Sesamoid” means shaped like a sesame seed. They protect the tendon and improve its leverage.

questions.prompt: What is the largest sesamoid bone in the body?
questions.explanation: The patella sits in the tendon of the quadriceps, in front of the knee.

figure.alt: The legs from the front, with the right patella in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which cells build new bone?
questions.explanation: Osteoblasts build: they lay down the collagen matrix that then mineralises.

questions.prompt: Which cells break down (resorb) bone?
questions.explanation: Osteoclasts “clear” bone. Large cells with many nuclei, they dissolve the matrix so bone can be reshaped and calcium released.

questions.prompt: What are mature bone cells, trapped in small spaces (lacunae) in the matrix they made, called?
questions.explanation: An osteoblast that has walled itself in becomes an osteocyte; it maintains the bone around it.

questions.prompt: What is the shaft of a long bone called?
What is each wider end of a long bone called?
questions.explanation: The epiphyses are filled with spongy bone and capped with articular cartilage where they form joints.

questions.prompt: In a child, what is the plate of hyaline cartilage where a long bone grows in length?
questions.explanation: It sits between the epiphysis and the diaphysis. When growth stops it turns to bone and leaves the epiphyseal line.

questions.prompt: What is the tough membrane that covers the outside of a bone, except where it forms a joint?
questions.explanation: Peri- means around. The periosteum carries blood vessels and nerves, and anchors tendons and ligaments.

questions.prompt: What is the hollow centre of a long bone’s shaft, filled with yellow marrow in adults, called?
Which tissue makes blood cells?
questions.explanation: Making blood cells is called haematopoiesis. In adults red marrow is mostly in flat bones, vertebrae, the hip bones and the upper ends of the femur and humerus.

questions.prompt: What is the basic structural unit of compact bone, rings of matrix around a central canal, called?
What runs through the centre of each osteon, carrying blood vessels and nerves?
questions.explanation: Perforating (Volkmann’s) canals run across the bone and link the central canals to each other and to the periosteum.

questions.prompt: What is the light bone made of a lattice of thin struts (trabeculae), found inside the ends of long bones, called?
questions.explanation: Its spaces hold red marrow. Compact bone forms the dense outer layer.

questions.prompt: By which process do the flat bones of the skull and the clavicles form, straight from sheets of connective tissue?
By which process do most bones form, replacing a model made of hyaline cartilage?
questions.explanation: Endo- (within) chondral (cartilage). Long bones, vertebrae and the base of the skull form this way.

questions.prompt: Which mineral makes bone hard?
questions.explanation: Crystals of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) give hardness; collagen fibres give flexibility, so bone doesn’t shatter.

questions.prompt: How many bones form the cranium, the part of the skull around the brain?
questions.explanation: Frontal, two parietal, two temporal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid.

questions.prompt: How many facial bones are there?
questions.explanation: Two each of nasal, maxilla, zygomatic, lacrimal, palatine and inferior nasal concha, plus the vomer and the mandible.

questions.prompt: How many bones make up the skull, not counting the ear ossicles and the hyoid?
questions.explanation: 8 cranial and 14 facial bones.

questions.prompt: Which is the only skull bone that moves freely?
questions.explanation: It moves at the temporomandibular joint, in front of each ear.

figure.alt: The skull from the left, with the mandible in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the large hole in the occipital bone where the spinal cord passes through?
questions.explanation: Latin for “great hole”.

questions.prompt: The skull rests on the atlas by which two bumps beside the foramen magnum?
questions.explanation: Nodding “yes” happens at this joint (atlanto-occipital).

questions.prompt: Which suture joins the frontal bone to the two parietal bones?
questions.explanation: It runs across the top of the head from side to side, where a crown would sit.

questions.prompt: Which suture joins the two parietal bones to each other?
questions.explanation: It runs front to back along the midline of the skull.

questions.prompt: Which suture joins the parietal bones to the occipital bone?
questions.explanation: Shaped like the Greek letter lambda (λ), at the back of the head.

questions.prompt: Which suture joins each parietal bone to the temporal bone below it?
questions.explanation: Squamous means scale-like: the thin temporal bone overlaps the parietal like a scale.

questions.prompt: What are the soft, membrane-covered gaps between the skull bones of a baby called?
questions.explanation: They let the skull squeeze through the birth canal and the brain grow. The largest, at the front, closes by about 18 months.

questions.prompt: What is the bony bump you can feel behind your ear?
questions.explanation: Part of the temporal bone; neck muscles such as the sternocleidomastoid attach to it.

figure.alt: The skull from the left, with the temporal bone in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Name the three ear ossicles.
questions.explanation: Hammer, anvil and stirrup. They carry vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.

questions.prompt: Which U-shaped bone in the neck does not form a joint with any other bone?
questions.explanation: Muscles and ligaments hold it in place under the mandible; it anchors the tongue and helps in swallowing.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the hyoid in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the saddle-shaped hollow in the sphenoid bone that holds the pituitary gland?
questions.explanation: Latin for “Turkish saddle”.

questions.prompt: Which part of the ethmoid bone is full of small holes for the nerves of smell?
questions.explanation: Cribriform means sieve-like.

questions.prompt: The mandible forms a joint with which bone?
questions.explanation: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ), just in front of the ear.

questions.prompt: Which two bones form the bony part of the nasal septum?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular plate of the ethmoid at the top, the vomer below; cartilage completes the septum at the front.

figure.alt: The skull, see-through, with the vomer in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which bones form the hard palate, the roof of the mouth?
questions.explanation: The palatine processes of the maxillae form the front three quarters, the palatine bones the back.

figure.alt: The skull from below, with the palatine bones in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which bone is the cheekbone?
questions.explanation: Its temporal process joins the zygomatic process of the temporal bone to form the zygomatic arch.

figure.alt: The skull from the left, with the zygomatic bone in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which butterfly-shaped cranial bone touches all the other cranial bones?
questions.explanation: It is called the keystone of the cranium. You can see its greater wing at the temple.

figure.alt: The skull from the left, with the sphenoid in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which bones form the upper jaw and hold the upper teeth?
questions.explanation: The two maxillae also form part of each orbit and the floor and sides of the nasal cavity.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many bones are in the adult vertebral column, counting the sacrum and the coccyx as one each?
questions.explanation: 24 separate vertebrae plus the sacrum and coccyx. Before fusion there are 33: 7 + 12 + 5 + 5 + 4.

questions.prompt: How many cervical vertebrae are there?
questions.explanation: Breakfast at 7, lunch at 12, dinner at 5: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar.

figure.alt: The vertebral column from the left, with the cervical vertebrae in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many thoracic vertebrae are there?
questions.explanation: One for each pair of ribs.

figure.alt: The vertebral column from the left, with the thoracic vertebrae in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many lumbar vertebrae are there?

figure.alt: The vertebral column from the left, with the lumbar vertebrae in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many vertebrae fuse to form the sacrum?
questions.explanation: The sacrum is a triangle of five fused vertebrae; the hip bones join it at the sacroiliac joints.

figure.alt: The vertebral column from the left, with the sacrum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the tailbone called?
questions.explanation: Usually four small fused vertebrae (three to five) below the sacrum.

questions.prompt: What is the first cervical vertebra (C1), which holds up the skull, called?
questions.explanation: Named after the Titan who held up the heavens. It has no body and no spinous process: it is a ring.

figure.alt: The top of the neck, with the atlas in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the second cervical vertebra (C2) called?
questions.explanation: The atlas turns around it when you shake your head “no”.

figure.alt: The top of the neck, with the axis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the tooth-like peg of the axis that the atlas turns around?
questions.explanation: Dens is Latin for tooth.

questions.prompt: Which vertebra’s long spinous process is the bump you can feel at the base of the neck?
questions.explanation: It is called the vertebra prominens and is a landmark for counting vertebrae.

figure.alt: The neck from the left, with C7 in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which vertebrae have holes in their transverse processes (transverse foramina) for the vertebral arteries?
Which vertebrae have facets where the ribs join them?
questions.explanation: Facets on the bodies take the heads of the ribs; facets on the transverse processes take the tubercles of the ribs (except ribs 11 and 12).

questions.prompt: Which vertebrae have the largest bodies?
questions.explanation: They carry the most weight.

questions.prompt: What is the hole in each vertebra that the spinal cord passes through?
questions.explanation: Stacked up, the vertebral foramina form the vertebral canal. Spinal nerves leave through the intervertebral foramina between neighbouring vertebrae.

questions.prompt: Which part of a vertebra points backwards and can be felt down the middle of the back?
What is the soft, gel-like centre of an intervertebral disc called?
questions.explanation: In a slipped (herniated) disc, the nucleus pulposus bulges out through a tear in the annulus.

figure.alt: The vertebral column from the left, with the intervertebral discs in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the tough outer ring of an intervertebral disc called?
Which two curves of the vertebral column are primary, there since before birth?
questions.explanation: They bend the same way as the whole spine of a curled-up fetus. The cervical curve develops as a baby lifts its head, the lumbar curve as it stands and walks.

questions.prompt: What is an exaggerated outward curve of the thoracic spine (a hunchback) called?
What is an exaggerated inward curve of the lumbar spine (swayback) called?
What is a sideways curve of the spine called?
Which bones are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The seven vertebrae of the neck.

questions.prompt: What are ribs 8 to 12 called, which do not join the sternum directly?

questions.prompt: Name the three parts of the sternum.

questions.prompt: What is the ridge where the manubrium meets the body of the sternum, level with the second ribs, called?
questions.explanation: It is the landmark for finding the second rib and counting ribs down from there.

questions.prompt: What is the dip at the top of the manubrium, between the clavicles, called?
What is the small pointed lower tip of the sternum called?
questions.explanation: Cartilage in young people, it slowly turns to bone. Xiphoid means sword-shaped.

figure.alt: The rib cage from the front, with the xiphoid process in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What joins the front ends of the upper ribs to the sternum?

questions.prompt: Which two bones form the pectoral (shoulder) girdle?
Which bone is the only bony link between the upper limb and the axial skeleton?
questions.explanation: It joins the manubrium at the sternoclavicular joint and the scapula at the acromioclavicular joint. It is one of the most often broken bones.

questions.prompt: What is the shallow socket on the scapula that the head of the humerus fits into?
questions.explanation: It is shallow, which is why the shoulder moves so freely and dislocates so easily.

questions.prompt: What is the bony point of the shoulder, the part of the scapula that joins the clavicle?
What is the hook-like process at the front of the scapula, below the clavicle?
questions.explanation: Coracoid means like a crow’s beak.

questions.prompt: Which is the bone of the upper arm?

figure.alt: The right arm, with the humerus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the humerus, just below its head, often breaks in falls?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve wraps around it, so it can be hurt in these fractures.

questions.prompt: You hit your “funny bone” when you knock the ulnar nerve against which bump of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The nerve runs in a groove behind the medial epicondyle, on the inner side of the elbow.

questions.prompt: Which forearm bone is on the thumb side?
questions.explanation: Radius and thumb both point outward. The radius turns around the ulna when you turn your palm down.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many metacarpals are in each hand?
questions.explanation: One for each finger, numbered 1 (thumb) to 5.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the metacarpals in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many phalanges are in each hand?
questions.explanation: Three in each finger and two in the thumb.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the phalanges in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many phalanges are in the thumb?
questions.explanation: A proximal and a distal phalanx; the fingers also have a middle one.

questions.prompt: Name the four carpals of the proximal row, from the thumb side.
questions.explanation: Some Lovers Try Positions That They Can’t Handle: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform (proximal row); trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate (distal row).

questions.prompt: Name the four carpals of the distal row, from the thumb side.
questions.explanation: Some Lovers Try Positions That They Can’t Handle. The distal row is the second half: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

questions.prompt: Which carpal bone is broken most often, usually in a fall on an outstretched hand?
questions.explanation: Its blood supply enters from the far end, so a break near the wrist can heal badly. Pain in the “anatomical snuffbox” at the base of the thumb is the sign.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the scaphoid in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which carpal bone sits at the base of the thumb?
questions.explanation: Trapezium for the thumb. Its saddle joint with the first metacarpal lets the thumb oppose the fingers.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest carpal bone?
questions.explanation: It sits in the middle of the wrist, below the middle finger.

questions.prompt: Which carpal bone has a hook on its palm side?
questions.explanation: Hamulus is Latin for little hook.

questions.prompt: Which pea-shaped carpal bone is a sesamoid bone in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris?
questions.explanation: Pisum is Latin for pea. You can feel it at the base of the palm on the little finger side.

questions.prompt: Joints are grouped by what holds them together. Name the three groups.
questions.explanation: Fibrous joints are held by dense connective tissue, cartilaginous joints by cartilage, and synovial joints have a fluid-filled cavity.

questions.prompt: The sutures of the skull are which kind of joint?
questions.explanation: They hardly move at all (synarthroses).

questions.prompt: The intervertebral discs and the pubic symphysis are which kind of joint?
questions.explanation: Joined by fibrocartilage, they move a little.

questions.prompt: What kind of joint holds a tooth in its socket?
questions.explanation: A fibrous joint: the periodontal ligament ties the tooth to the jaw.

questions.prompt: What is the fluid that lubricates freely moving joints called?
questions.explanation: The synovial membrane lining the joint capsule makes it.

questions.prompt: What covers the ends of the bones inside a synovial joint?
questions.explanation: Smooth hyaline cartilage, so the bones glide over each other.

questions.prompt: The shoulder and hip are which type of synovial joint?
questions.explanation: They move in every direction, and rotate.

questions.prompt: The elbow and the knee are mainly which type of synovial joint?
questions.explanation: They bend and straighten in one plane, like a door.

questions.prompt: Which type of joint between the atlas and the axis lets you shake your head “no”?
questions.explanation: The ring of the atlas turns around the dens. The joint between the tops of the radius and ulna is a pivot too.

questions.prompt: The joint at the base of the thumb, between the trapezium and the first metacarpal, is which type?
questions.explanation: Both surfaces are shaped like saddles, which lets the thumb move across the palm to touch the fingers (opposition).

questions.prompt: The wrist joint (radiocarpal) and the knuckles are which type of synovial joint?
questions.explanation: An oval surface in an oval socket: they bend and move side to side, but don’t rotate.

questions.prompt: The joints between the carpal bones are which type, where flat surfaces slide over each other?
What joins bone to bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone.

questions.prompt: What joins muscle to bone?
questions.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.prompt: Which ligament inside the knee stops the tibia sliding forward under the femur?
questions.explanation: Cruciate means crossed: the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments cross inside the knee.

questions.prompt: What are the two C-shaped pads of fibrocartilage in the knee that cushion the femur on the tibia?
questions.explanation: One medial, one lateral. Twisting the bent knee can tear them.
